answer.evidence: The whole object is drawn face-on. Rows 5-7 are a brown crossbar at the top of a light grey frame, with a light line at row 8. It reads as a front-facing beam, not a horizontal surface. Rows 9-26 show the stacked chairs only as vertical bands of dark and mid brown, so no chair seat is seen from above. The cart base at rows 27-29 has a 1-row light top edge and no real top plane. No ellipse, roof or visible container contents appear, so the stack looks like a flat front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small, narrow sprite, about one tile wide. It has 11 distinct colours, the same as prop-hedge (11) and not far below prop-bench-wood and prop-lamp-crook (14 each). Its median of 10 colours per 16x16 tile equals the hedge's, and its 0% 5x5 flat-fill coverage matches the references. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outline leans toward the material tone rather than the neutral black or grey line of the 'sticker' look (the lamp is 100% neutral). The repeated chair-leg and seat stripes and the cart body show about 4 lightness steps, a little fewer than Beodeul's 5-6. It is simpler than the stall and well, but it is on par with the small thin props, so the verdict is a modest pass.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small, narrow prop, about one tile wide and one and a half tall. It has 11 distinct colours and a median of 10 colours per full tile, matching prop-hedge (11 colours, 10 per tile) and well above the sparse bench and lamp, which read 0 per tile. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so there are no large single-colour areas. 0% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline leans toward a tint of the neighbouring material rather than a black sticker line, as in the hedge. The chair bars and cart read as roughly 4 stepped tones with banding and highlight dots. That is a little shallower than the 5-6 steps on the big stall and well references, and its total colour count is far below their 38-40. For a thin, sparse stack of folded chairs this is acceptable next to the hedge and bench, and a careful artist would not see it as noticeably flatter or more sticker-like. I judged this by eye because the piece is small and low-contrast.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small, thin grey and brown cart with stacked chairs. The measured facts are mixed. It has 0% flat-fill coverage and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so its outline is tinted, not a black sticker line. Its median of 10 colours per tile matches the hedge reference. However, it has only 11 distinct colours across several materials (metal pipes, a wooden or metal cart bed, wheels). That leaves about 3 lightness steps per material, against about 5-6 in the richer references (stall-cheese has 40 colours, well-roofed 38). The pipes and cart read as flat-shaded with little per-part highlighting, grain or texture dots. A multi-part object like this should carry more variation than the plain hedge, which has the same 11 colours. Next to the stall and well it looks thinner and flatter, so I fail it under the 'when in doubt, fail' rule.
